q: Who gave the call "Dilli Chalo" to the soldiers of the Azad Hind Fauj?

n: He united the princely states into the Indian Union.

q: Who was the first President of India?
n: He was President from 1950 to 1962.

q: Who gave the slogan "Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan"?
n: He gave it in 1965. He was the second Prime Minister of India.

q: What is the national animal of India?
n: The Royal Bengal tiger.

q: What is the national bird of India?
n: Its proper name is the Indian peafowl.

q: What is the national flower of India?
n: The lotus grows in water and stands for purity in Indian culture.

q: What is the national tree of India?
n: Its branches send down roots that grow into new trunks, so one tree can spread over a wide area.

q: What is the national fruit of India?
n: The mango is often called the king of fruits.

q: Who wrote the national song "Vande Mataram"?
n: It appears in his novel Anandamath.

q: About how long does it take to sing the full national anthem?

q: The national calendar of India is based on which era?

q: Who designed the symbol of the Indian rupee (₹)?

q: Who was the first woman Prime Minister of India?

q: Who was the first woman President of India?

q: Who was the first Indian to go into space?

q: Who was the first woman of Indian origin to go into space?
n: She first flew in 1997 on the space shuttle Columbia.

n: She was appointed to the Supreme Court in 1989.

q: Who was the first Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
n: He was Speaker of the first Lok Sabha, from 1952.

q: Which was the first full-length Indian feature film?

n: She won a bronze in weightlifting at Sydney in 2000.

n: He later became the second President. His birthday, 5 September, is Teachers' Day.

n: A person with AB positive blood can receive red cells from all groups.

q: Which is the hottest planet?

n: Iron oxide, or rust, in its soil gives Mars a reddish colour.

q: Which planet is best known for its bright rings?
n: The rings are made of pieces of ice and rock.

q: Which planet is called the Blue Planet?

q: Which planet is called the morning star or the evening star?
n: Venus is the brightest object in the night sky after the Moon.

q: What is the name of the galaxy we live in?

n: Hydrogen is also the most plentiful element in the universe.

n: It is the tallest kind of grass.

q: In which city are the headquarters of the International Olympic Committee?
n: Lausanne is in Switzerland.

q: What is the chemical symbol of gold?
n: It comes from the Latin name aurum.

q: What is the chemical symbol of silver?
n: It comes from the Latin name argentum.

q: What is the chemical symbol of iron?
n: It comes from the Latin name ferrum.

q: What is the chemical symbol of sodium?
n: It comes from the Latin name natrium.

q: What is the chemical symbol of potassium?
n: It comes from the Latin name kalium.

q: What is the atomic number of hydrogen?
n: Hydrogen is the first element of the periodic table.

q: Which is the most plentiful element in the Earth's crust?
n: Silicon comes second.

q: Which is the most plentiful metal in the Earth's crust?
n: It is obtained from an ore called bauxite.

q: Who arranged the elements in the first widely used periodic table?
n: He published it in 1869 and left gaps for elements not yet found.

q: How many elements are there in the modern periodic table?
n: The last of them were made in laboratories.

q: What is the pH value of pure water?
n: A pH below 7 is acidic and a pH above 7 is basic.

q: Which acid is found in lemons and oranges?
n: It gives citrus fruits their sour taste.

q: Which acid is found in vinegar?
n: Vinegar is a weak solution of this acid in water.

q: Which acid is found in curd and sour milk?
n: Bacteria in the milk produce it.

q: What is the chemical name of baking soda?
n: Washing soda is sodium carbonate.

q: Which gas is known as laughing gas?
n: Dentists and surgeons have long used it to dull pain.

q: Which light gas that does not burn is used to fill party balloons and airships?
n: Hydrogen is lighter still, but it catches fire easily.

q: Dry ice is the solid form of which gas?
n: It turns straight from a solid into a gas without melting.

q: Brass is an alloy of which two metals?
n: An alloy is a mixture of a metal with other elements.

q: Bronze is an alloy of which two metals?
n: It gave its name to the Bronze Age.

q: Which is the smallest prime number?
n: It is also the only even prime number. The number 1 is not counted as prime.

q: Which Indian mathematician of the 7th century gave rules for calculating with zero?
n: He treated zero as a number in its own right.

q: What is the value of pi, correct to two decimal places?
n: The fraction 22/7 is a close value often used in school.

q: Pi is the circumference of a circle divided by its what?
n: The answer is the same for every circle, large or small.

q: What is the distance around a circle called?
n: It is the perimeter of the circle.

q: What is the sum of the angles of a triangle?
n: This is true of every triangle drawn on a flat surface.

q: What is the sum of the angles of a quadrilateral?
n: A quadrilateral can be cut into two triangles: 180° and 180°.

q: How many degrees are there in a right angle?
n: The corner of a square is a right angle.

q: How many sides does a hexagon have?
n: The cells of a honeycomb are hexagons.

q: What is a polygon with eight sides called?
n: Think of an octopus, which has eight arms.

q: What is the longest side of a right-angled triangle called?
n: It is the side opposite the right angle.

q: The rule a² + b² = c² for a right-angled triangle is named after whom?
n: The same rule is found in the ancient Indian Sulba Sutras of Baudhayana.

q: Who is called the father of geometry?
n: His book is called the "Elements".

q: Which Roman numeral stands for 50?
n: C stands for 100 and X for 10.

q: Which Roman numeral stands for 1,000?
n: D stands for 500.

q: How many zeros are there in one lakh?
n: One lakh is written 1,00,000.

q: How many zeros are there in one crore?
n: One crore is written 1,00,00,000.

q: One million is equal to how many lakhs?
n: One million is 10,00,000. Ten million make one crore.

q: Which number is known as the Hardy-Ramanujan number?
n: It is the smallest number that is the sum of two cubes in two different ways.

q: On which date is National Mathematics Day observed in India?
n: It is the birthday of Srinivasa Ramanujan.
